Antidotum hoc breue parare, quo ostendere,
caussam nullam esse, cur exemplis huiusmodi
quisquam à constantia moueri, aut in agnita
veritate percelli debeat.
Quam quidem ad rem, ante omnia locus
iam allatus Apostoli facit. Etenim cùm Spi-
ritus S. in verbo suo futurum prædixerit, vt
quidam à fide defcifcant; quid miraris eueni-
re, quod Spiritus S. tanto iam ante tempore
euenturum nunciarat?
Quin potius constantiæ ac fortitudinis ar-
gumentum hinc tibi petendum; quòd tanto
firmius ac fidelius indubitato Dei Verbo ad-
hærere debeas, cuius veritas, vt in aliis innu-
meris, ita etiam hoc in loco, euentu euidentis-
simo clarissimoque probata sit.
Maximè verò te non turbabit ifthæc ho-
minum ieuissimorum inconstantia & defe-
ctio; si consideraueris Deum Opt. Max. non
sine iustissimis caussis, hujus generis offersio-
nes seu scandala, in Ecclesia sua permittere.
Sunt autem duæ potissimum: quarum altera
Electos ipsos seu filios Dei: altera verò im-
pios, potissimum autem Apostatas ipsos, at-
tingit.

note.i: Causæ propter quas Deus Apostasiæ peccatum permittit.

page.notes: Left margin note: the reference mark for it is not visible in the text, so it is placed at the paragraph beside which it stands. "tuibari" is a doubtful reading of a word split by a small gap. The note's italic type is read as printed. The catchword "cio" is the start of the next page's word, shown at the right below the last line. The text is copied as printed; the long s has been rendered as s and ff as ss only where the ligature was clear.
